chunks: Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh from his father from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from his father from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
The testimony of women is not valid in the hudud (fixed punishments) nor in al-qawd (retaliatory execution for murder).
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women valid in hudud and qawd cases according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on testimonies (Bayinat) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes the exclusion of women's testimony in Hudud and Qawd, reflecting the juristic view that these categories require the rigor of male witnesses due to the severity of the punishments. While some schools accept female testimony in Hudud, this narration highlights the Shia position that the specific evidentiary standards for fixed punishments and retribution do not accommodate the dual-witness model typically applied to women in other civil matters.
